query: For refractory materials, experiments at the solid-to-fluid transition are difficult and yield sparse, scattered data, while the large compositional space of high-entropy systems makes systematic screening impractical. DFT free-energy studies can determine the transition from the crossing of solid and dense-fluid Gibbs energies and provide associated thermodynamic properties, but their reliance on extensive ab initio molecular dynamics makes them costly. TOR-TILD has shown high efficiency for elemental and binary systems, yet becomes substantially slower for multicomponent systems. Any broadly useful approach must retain ab initio-level accuracy, represent all thermodynamic effects identified as important, treat both phases around the transition, and remain practical across relevant compositions and temperatures. For a multicomponent high-entropy material in these high-temperature states, what single intervention could improve determination of transition temperature, fusion enthalpy and entropy, volume change, and dense-fluid heat capacity? Formulate one hypothesis specifying the intervention and causal mechanism, its predicted outcome relative to existing experimental and computational baselines, its boundary conditions, supporting prior evidence, and a decisive experiment or benchmark that would falsify it.

generation.hypothesis: The incorporation of deep learning potentials, such as DeepMD, into the simulation of high-entropy alloys can improve the determination of transition temperature, fusion enthalpy and entropy, volume change, and dense-fluid heat capacity.

generation.intervention: Incorporation of deep learning potentials into simulations
generation.mechanism: Improved prediction of thermodynamic properties through enhanced representation of structural and chemical complexity
generation.predicted_outcome: More accurate determination of transition temperature, fusion enthalpy and entropy, volume change, and dense-fluid heat capacity
generation.baseline: Existing experimental and computational methods, such as DFT and CALPHAD
generation.boundary: Applicability limited to high-entropy alloys with complex chemical and structural properties
generation.uncertainty: Uncertainty remains regarding the transferability of deep learning potentials to different alloy systems and the accuracy of predictions for specific properties

falsification_experiment.design: Comparison of predicted thermodynamic properties using deep learning potentials with experimental measurements for a range of high-entropy alloys
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the predicted properties deviate significantly from experimental measurements, the hypothesis is falsified

Melting simulations of high-entropy carbonitrides by deep learning potentials

Abstract: The melting temperature is a crucial property of materials that determines their potential applications in different industrial fields. In this study, we used a deep neural network potential to describe the structure of high-entropy (TiZrTaHfNb)CxN1−x carbonitrides (HECN) in both solid and liquid states. This approach allows us to predict heating and cooling temperatures depending on the nitrogen content to determine the melting temperature and analyze structure changes from atomistic point of view. A steady increase in nitrogen content leads to increasing melting temperature, with a maximum approaching for 25% of nitrogen in the HECN. A careful analysis of pair correlations, together with calculations of entropy in the considered liquid phases of HECNs allows us to explain the origin of the nonlinear enhancement of the melting temperature with increasing nitrogen content. The maximum melting temperature of 3580 ± 30 K belongs to (TiZrTaHfNb)C0.75N0.25 composition. Computational property predictions of Ta–Nb–Hf–Zr high-entropy alloys

Abstract: Refractory high entropy alloys (R-HEAs) are becoming prominent in recent years because of their properties and uses as high strength and high hardness materials for ambient and high temperature, aerospace and nuclear radiation tolerance applications, orthopedic applications etc. The mechanical properties like yield strength and ductility of TaNbHfZr R-HEA depend on the local nanostructure and chemical ordering, which in term depend on the annealing treatment. In this study we have computationally obtained various properties of the equimolar TaNbHfZr alloy like the role of configurational entropy in the thermodynamic property, rate of evolution of nanostructure morphology in thermally annealed systems, dislocation simulation based quantitative prediction of yield strength, nature of dislocation movement through short range clustering (SRC) and qualitative prediction of ductile to brittle transition behavior.
